questions.q: Which of these is one of the five valid accounting period statuses in Oracle Fusion?
options: Future Enterable
Pending Approval
Draft
Archived
questions.explain: The five statuses are Never Opened, Future Enterable, Open, Closed, and Permanently Closed.

questions.q: What does the 'Permanently Closed' period status mean?
options: The period can still be reopened with manager approval
The period is closed for final, audit-integrity reasons and cannot be reopened
It is the same as 'Never Opened'
It only applies to secondary ledgers
questions.explain: Permanently Closed is the final status, preventing any further reopening to preserve audit integrity.

questions.q: What must already be in place before you can open a ledger's first accounting period?
options: Only a business unit, with no legal entity required
Nothing; periods can be opened independently of any other setup
The calendar defined and assigned, the ledger created with chart of accounts and currency, and at least one legal entity assigned
Only a chart of accounts, with no ledger required
questions.explain: Opening the first period depends on the calendar, ledger, and legal entity assignments already being correctly configured.

questions.q: What is the typical order periods move through over their lifetime?
options: Closed, then Never Opened, then Open
There is no typical order; statuses are assigned randomly
Permanently Closed, then Open, then Never Opened
Never Opened (or Future Enterable), then Open, then Closed, then eventually Permanently Closed
questions.explain: Periods generally progress from Never Opened or Future Enterable, to Open, to Closed, and eventually to Permanently Closed once audits are complete.

questions.q: Why is managing period status described as a day-to-day control rather than a one-time setup step?
options: Because period status never changes once set
Because a controller must actively open and close periods every accounting cycle as business activity and reconciliations proceed
Because period status is set automatically by the chart of accounts
Because only secondary ledgers require ongoing period management
questions.explain: Unlike one-time structural setup, period status requires ongoing attention each accounting cycle to open the next period and close the completed one appropriately.
